deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G is a finite group of substitutions (permutations). T = Σψ is a subgroup ("Divisor") of G, and G = T + Tθ_1 + … + Tθ_{p-1} is its decomposition into right cosets, so p = [G:T].

Claim 1 (no extra hypothesis). Let θ ∈ G and let n ≥ 1 be least with θ^n ∈ T. Then the cosets H: T, Tθ, …, Tθ^{n-1} are pairwise distinct. [Implicit, mine: Tθ^a = Tθ^b iff θ^{a-b} ∈ T, and 0 < |a-b| < n contradicts minimality.] So either n = p, or n < p.

Claim 2. Suppose n < p. Pick θ' ∈ G not in the union of H. Then the cosets H': Tθ', Tθθ', …, Tθ^{n-1}θ' are pairwise distinct and disjoint from H. [Mine: distinctness among themselves follows from Claim 1 by right multiplication by θ'.] Disjointness from H: if ψ'θ^{s'}θ' = ψθ^s, then
θ' = θ^{-s'}ψ'^{-1}ψθ^s = (θ^{-s'}ψ'^{-1}ψθ^{s'})·θ^{s-s'} = ψ''θ^h.
This contradicts the choice of θ'. The step requires that θ^{-1}ψθ is again some ψ, i.e. θ^{-1}Tθ = T. Dedekind states this assumption explicitly, and in the right-hand margin writes Tθ = θT for 'our case'. [Mine: h = s - s' is reduced mod n using θ^n ∈ T.]

Claim 3 (assuming θT = Tθ). For any θ', θ'' the 'rows' H' = {Tθ^kθ'} and H'' = {Tθ^kθ''} (k = 0..n-1) are either identical or disjoint. Suppose they share an element: ψ'θ^{s'}θ' = ψ''θ^{s''}θ''. Then θ' = θ^{-s'}ψ'^{-1}ψ''θ^{s''}θ'' = ψθ^sθ'' with s = s'' - s' (using normality). Hence H' = {Tθ^kψθ^sθ''}. Using the commutation rule, written as ψθ = θψ_1 (several crossed-out attempts at its form appear on the page), the ψ can be moved left into T. This gives H' = Tθ^sθ'', Tθ^{s±1}θ'', …, i.e. the same n cosets as H'' (exponents run through a full residue system mod n).

Conclusion. Taking θ', θ'', … successively from G, G is partitioned into disjoint rows, each consisting of exactly n cosets of T. Therefore n | p.

Modern form: if θ normalizes T, then T⟨θ⟩ is a subgroup with [T⟨θ⟩ : T] = n. The rows are the right cosets of T⟨θ⟩ in G, each a union of n cosets of T, so n divides [G:T]. Equivalently: the order of θT in N_G(T)/T divides [G:T] when T ⊴ G.

The next page ('Nochmals') redoes the argument cleanly. It notes that Claim 1 needs no normality, while Claim 3 does.

Context. On the previous page Dedekind studies the Galois-theoretic decomposition f(x) = Π f_i(x, ρ) over a normal ('Galois') resolvent. This lemma on index divisibility serves that group-theoretic analysis of the Galois group and its subgroups.
errors: In the final display Dedekind writes H' = Tθ^sθ'', Tθ^{s-1}θ'', Tθ^{s-2}θ'', …, Tθ^{s-(n-1)}θ''. Correctly, Tθ^kψθ^sθ'' = Tψ_kθ^{k+s}θ'' = Tθ^{s+k}θ'', so the exponents should increase (s, s+1, …, s+n-1), not decrease. The slip is harmless: both lists run through all residues mod n, so the set equals H''.
The derivation in Claim 2 silently reduces h = s - s' modulo n using θ^n ∈ T. This is fine but unstated.

The normality hypothesis (θ^{-1}Tθ = T) is genuinely necessary for n | p and Dedekind correctly flags it. Counterexample without it: G = S3, T = <(12)>, θ = (13) gives n = 2 and p = 3. The derivation of 'θ' = ψθ^sθ''' in Claim 3 is compressed but correct under that hypothesis.
Several crossed-out lines attempt to fix the form of the commutation rule (θψ = ψ_1θ vs ψθ = θψ_1). The page is a working draft; the fair copy is on the next page.

results.what: Cosets T, Tθ, …, Tθ^{n-1} are distinct, where n is the least positive integer with θ^n ∈ T.
If θ normalizes T, the 'rows' {Tθ^kθ'} partition G, hence n divides p = [G:T].
results.modern_name: Lagrange's theorem applied to T⟨θ⟩ ⊇ T; the order of θT in N(T)/T divides [G:T]
results.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1771) / Cauchy, Galois (1830s); coset form standard in Jordan (1870)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine coset-counting argument (Lagrange's theorem for T⟨θ⟩ with T normalized by θ). Dedekind's group-theoretic treatment of Galois theory in his Göttingen lectures (c. 1856–58) is known and discussed (Scharlau, Haubrich, Corry). The only notable features are the explicit flagging of the normality hypothesis and the draft-level sign slip.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation, PermutationGroup; from sympy.combinatorics.named_groups import SymmetricGroup; G=SymmetricGroup(4); T=PermutationGroup([Permutation([[0,1],[2,3]],size=4),Permutation([[0,2],[1,3]],size=4)]); th=Permutation([[0,1,2]],size=4); n=next(k for k in range(1,25) if T.contains(th**k)); p=G.order()//T.order(); (n, p, p % n == 0)
checkable.asserts: With T = Klein four (normal in S4) and θ a 3-cycle: n = 3, p = 6, and n divides p.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation, PermutationGroup; from sympy.combinatorics.named_groups import SymmetricGroup; G=SymmetricGroup(3); T=PermutationGroup([Permutation([[0,1]],size=3)]); th=Permutation([[0,2]],size=3); n=next(k for k in range(1,7) if T.contains(th**k)); p=G.order()//T.order(); (n, p, p % n == 0)
checkable.asserts: Without normality the conclusion fails: n = 2, p = 3, 2 does not divide 3. This confirms that Dedekind's hypothesis θ^{-1}Tθ = T is needed.

checkable.sympy: from sympy.combinatorics import Permutation, PermutationGroup; from sympy.combinatorics.named_groups import SymmetricGroup; T=PermutationGroup([Permutation([[0,1],[2,3]],size=4),Permutation([[0,2],[1,3]],size=4)]); th=Permutation([[0,1,2]],size=4); all(T.contains(th**-1*g*th) for g in T.generate())
checkable.asserts: θ normalizes T in the first example (θ^{-1}ψθ ∈ T for all ψ ∈ T).

transcription_corrections: Final display: the manuscript indeed reads Tθ^sθ'', Tθ^{s-1}θ'', Tθ^{s-2}θ'', …, Tθ^{s-(n-1)}θ''. This is Dedekind's own sign slip, not a transcription error.
Right-hand marginal note: 'In unserm Fall anstandenn[?]' is probably 'In unserem Fall anzuwenden' (or similar) before 'Tθ = θT'. The reading is uncertain.
'Complexe' before the list (H) is plausible; the word may also be read 'Complexen'.
Crossed-out lines near the bottom: they read roughly 'oder wenn von ψθ = θψ_1' with struck attempts 'θψ = ψ_1θ, θ^2' and 'θψ_1 = ψ_2θ'. These are working attempts at the commutation rule.
